title: Lying Leg Curl
summary: Face-down leg curl: hamstrings 1. With the hip straight, the hamstrings work at a shorter length than in the seated curl.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: lying leg curl machine or attachment.

muscles.why: The hamstrings bend the knee. Lying flat keeps the hip straight, so they are shorter than when seated, where the hip is bent.

region_notes.text: Seated leg curls grew the hamstrings more than lying leg curls.

muscles.why: The gastrocnemius crosses the knee and helps bend it; below the counting floor (0.2).

setup.text: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot, just off the end of the pad.
Pad on the lower calves, just above the heels.
Hold the handles and keep the hips pressed down.

form_cues.cue: Keep hips pressed into the pad
form_cues.why: Hips down keeps the hamstrings, not the lower back, doing the lift.

form_cues.cue: Curl the heels toward your glutes
form_cues.why: Curling fully brings the heels close to the glutes.
Lowering to near-straight knees is the stretch.

form_cues.cue: Point the toes slightly down if your calves cramp
form_cues.why: The gastrocnemius helps bend the knee; pointing the foot takes some of it out.

bias_tweaks.change: A pillow or wedge under the hips, or a machine with an angled pad
bias_tweaks.effect: Bends the hip a little, which lengthens the hamstrings.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Lifting the hips to start the curl.
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips pinned; lighten the load if they lift.

mistakes.text: Hips lifting to start the curl.
mistakes.fix: Press the hips into the pad.
Lower until the knees are nearly straight.

misconceptions.myth: Lying and seated leg curls work the hamstrings equally.
misconceptions.reality: Seated curls grew the hamstrings more.

misconceptions.myth: Machines don't build muscle like free weights.
misconceptions.reality: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth in a meta-analysis. Pick by fit, stability and how well you can push close to failure.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Machine isolation; low-risk to push close to failure.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Hip bent, so the hamstrings work longer; grew them more.
One leg at a time standing.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Bodyweight knee curl, lowering only; very hard.
Hip hinge with dumbbells for the hamstrings.

notes: Seated vs lying curl finding is one 12-week MRI study.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
